query: Use the planning majlis to plan adding per-user rate limiting to this notes API. Feature mode. Roles: core only. Write the workspace under planning/rate-limit/.
expected_behavior: Writes planning/rate-limit/00-brief.md with a Roster section naming exactly the five core roles, and does not ask which roles to seat (the request named them).
Writes 01-recon.md whose facts cite app.py lines.
Starts the critic groups as parallel subagents (or states that the harness has none and runs them in sequence), and the critiques say the reviewers wrote none of the material.
Writes record.md with DR headings, a resolution ledger with a Status column, and a scorecard.md with one row per core role.
Runs scripts/gate.py on the workspace and quotes its result; does not declare a pass the script did not print.
Any limit or threshold it proposes (requests per minute, window) is either sourced, given a stated method, or recorded as an owner decision with a default; no invented performance figures.
Ends with a plain-language hand-off listing owner decisions with their defaults.

query: Plan a small web app where staff book meeting rooms from their phones, using the planning majlis.
expected_behavior: Names the five core roles as always seated.
Proposes the optional roles with a reason each, recommending at least ux and end-user for a phone-facing web app.
Asks the user which optional roles to seat and stops to wait, without starting recon, tracks or subagents.
Mentions that a full run costs far more tokens than a normal chat, or asks/infers the mode, before starting.

query: Continue the planning majlis in planning/notes-export. Are we done?
expected_behavior: Runs scripts/gate.py on planning/notes-export and reports that the gate did not pass: security at 8 and XB-security-chaos-1 OPEN.
Does not say the plan is done or write deliverables.
Starts (or proposes, if it must ask) an emergency drill on XB-security-chaos-1 that adds a DR, bumps the record to v3, and is followed by a security re-score by a fresh critic.
